speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Manpower since the inception of the Silver Support Scheme in 2016 (a) how many Singaporeans who initially received payouts were assessed to be ineligible in subsequent years; (b) what support does the Scheme give to those between the bottom 20% to 30% of elderly Singaporeans; and (c) whether the Scheme's criteria for household monthly income per capita of $1,100 will be reviewed to exclude the income of the applicant's siblings living at the same address.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Coverage may, however, extend to include up to the next 10% of elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Recipients living in smaller flat types receive higher payouts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The automatic means-test assessment is done annually to take into account changes in circumstances of the elderly, to ensure Silver Support reaches those with lesser means as the Scheme was intended to do.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overall, the number of elderly eligible for Silver Support and the total annual amount paid out to recipients have been increasing each year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also continue to assess appeals from those who have missed the income criteria on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first is, I would like her to clarify whether the scheme target group remains the same.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In other words, is it still targeted at the bottom 20% of the elderly, with some support for those between 20% and 30%?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Because lately, some of the collaterals, including replies that we have received from the agency, do not seem to mention this second group of those between the bottom 20% and 30%.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like the Minister to clarify whether this group between the bottom 20% and 30% is still within the target of the scheme.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Minister has earlier said that the Ministry will review from time to time the relevance of the means testing criteria.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, it would be good for the scheme to look at those cases on a more generous basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On sibling income, I should give a little bit of background as to why we used per capita household income.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The whole idea is that if people are living in the same household, it is more reasonable to expect that they are providing mutual support to each other.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are, of course, other ways of measuring a person's level of support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You could, for example, include their family members who do not live in the same household.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But having considered the different options and assessed which one of it is more intrusive to establish, we finally settled on using the household income.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I accept the fact that within the same household, the level of support may not be identical.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, for those who are non-family members, in other words, for example, they are unrelated people living in the same household, we do not include their income.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if they are related, including siblings, their incomes are included.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, if on a case-by-case basis, there is reason for us to consider otherwise, then we will also assess them.
